title: Does Compression Imply Generalization? A Minimum Description Length Perspective
abstract: arXiv:2610.21376v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A central question in modern learning theory is what notion of compression, if any, explains why over-parameterized neural networks generalize. Existing answers measure complexity at different levels, ranging from weights to representations; however, estimating the associated quantities either requires held-out data in principle or relies on the challenging (ultra) high-dimensional mutual information estimation. To overcome these challenges, we approach the question through the minimum description length (MDL) principle, and specifically, we propose the prequential regret as a complementary signal that is computable from the training trajectory alone. We establish that, in the (nearly) interpolating regime, the expected prequential regret upper-bounds the description length of the trained parameter under the algorithm-induced distribution, and that this description length translates into a high-probability generalization bound in the PAC

translated_title: 压缩是否意味着泛化？基于最小描述长度的视角
translated_abstract: 现代学习理论的一个核心问题是：什么样的压缩概念（如果存在的话）能够解释过参数化神经网络为何具有泛化能力。现有的答案在不同的层面上衡量复杂度，范围从权重到表示；然而，估计这些相关量在原则上要么需要保留数据，要么依赖于极具挑战性的（超）高维互信息估计。为了克服这些挑战，我们通过最小描述长度原则来研究这个问题；具体而言，我们提出了预quential后悔，作为一种仅从训练轨迹即可计算的补充信号。我们证明，在（近乎）插值的情况下，期望预quential后悔在算法诱导分布下对训练后参数的描述长度给出了上界，并且该描述长度可以转化为PAC意义下的高概率泛化界。
tldr: 本文基于最小描述长度原则提出仅由训练轨迹即可计算的预quential后悔，证明其在（近乎）插值情况下上界了训练参数在算法诱导分布下的描述长度，进而转化为PAC高概率泛化界，为“压缩是否意味着泛化”提供了无需保留数据或互信息估计的新答案。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes the prequential regret—computable from the training trajectory alone—as an MDL-based signal that upper-bounds the description length of trained parameters in the (nearly) interpolating regime and translates into a high-probability PAC generalization bound, offering a new answer to whether compression implies generalization.
